subject: PD brief 18 – 25 Oct 2026: 56 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days were dominated by cardiac arrest and resuscitation — from pulse check duration and AED pad application to bystander CPR programs — alongside a strong paediatric thread on recognising sick kids early. Ventilation quality also featured twice, with real-time feedback showing measurable gains.
synthesis.discussion: Given that pad application eats most AED time and short pulse checks track with better ROSC, what single habit at your next arrest would you and your partner change first — and how would you know if it made a difference?

lessons.text: Pulse checks kept under 5 seconds were associated with higher ROSC (36.3% vs 19.5%) compared with 6 to 10 second checks — a prompt to brief your partner on check timing before the next arrest.
Across 8,115 AED activations, pad application took a median 42 seconds and accounted for 81% of the power-on-to-analysis interval — coaching bystanders to get pads on fast is where the time is won.

A French stepped-wedge trial of dispatcher training plus a volunteer responder app saw bystander CPR rise from 61.4% to 70.9%, though the effect weakened on adjustment and survival didn't improve — telephone-assisted CPR still seems worth every second.

Real-time feedback markedly improved ventilation quality in both adult arrest (68% vs 42% of breaths in guideline range) and paediatric simulation (87% vs 16.2% guideline-recommended tidal volume) — suggests feedback devices deserve a place in your next arrest workflow discussion.

Five scene findings independently flagged children who needed blood within 4 hours of ED arrival, with a high-risk tier capturing over a third of early transfusions — a useful lens for paediatric trauma pattern recognition on scene.

deep_dives.topic: Arrest efficiency: checks, pads and CPR
deep_dives.why: Three high-transferability papers this period all point at seconds lost in the first minutes of arrest care, each at a different link in the chain — pulse checks, pad application and bystander CPR. Together they offer a concrete way to audit your own crew's arrest timing.
questions: How would you actually time a pulse check to stay under 5 seconds during a noisy, compressed arrest?
Where in your last arrest did the biggest delay sit — recognition, pads, or compressions?
Does the registry caveat that quicker checks may mark healthier arrests change how much weight you give the ROSC finding?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how each paper measures 'time' — pulse check duration, power-on-to-pad interval, CPR before arrival — and consider which of those you could realistically observe or influence at your next arrest.

deep_dives.why: Two independent studies, one in adult arrest and one in paediatric simulation, both found feedback technology transformed ventilation quality from well under half of breaths in range to the large majority. With hyperventilation a longstanding resus problem, this is worth an hour before it reaches your service's equipment conversations.
questions: How confident are you in your own tidal volume and rate without any feedback?
Both studies are simulation or before-after designs — what would you need to see before calling feedback devices practice-changing?
Does the paediatric manikin finding transfer to the real small airways you ventilate on scene?
deep_dives.ideas: Consider whether the ventilation targets used in the two studies match what your local guideline defines as good BVM ventilation, and look at what feedback (visual, audible, instructor) you currently get in training versus on the road.

deep_dives.why: A registry study found scene predictors of early paediatric transfusion, while a scoping review found no operational definition of prehospital paediatric deterioration exists at all. Together they raise the question of how we identify sick children before hospital numbers arrive.
questions: What cues do you actually use to decide a child is deteriorating, and how do they compare with the study's five predictors?
If no operational definition of prehospital deterioration exists, what does your local guideline implicitly ask you to rely on?
The transfusion study excluded children missing prehospital vitals — how does that shape your reading of its tiers?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the study's five predictors against the triggers in your local paediatric guideline, and consider how you would recognise deterioration over time when the evidence base leans on single-timepoint vital signs.

papers.title: Airway strategy and survival in Polish HEMS
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 8,980 adults requiring advanced airway management
papers.finding: HEMS-performed intubation was the most common strategy (49.8%); sequential supraglottic-to-intubation did not differ significantly from HEMS-performed intubation in non-traumatic cardiac arrest; 32.9% were not alive at hospital handover

papers.title: Five scene findings flag kids needing blood
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort with decision-tree (CART) analysis
papers.n: 79,764 EMS-transported children aged 1–15
papers.finding: All five predictors independently predicted blood within 4 h of ED arrival; low/intermediate/high CART tiers had 1.2%/6.1%/36.7% transfusion rates, and the high-risk tier captured 36.8% of all early transfusions

papers.title: Ditch lights and sirens for fall-alarm calls
papers.design: Retrospective pre-post interventional analysis with interrupted time series
papers.n: 3,262 PERS activations (1,634 pre, 1,628 post)
papers.finding: L&S response fell from 98% to 12% of calls and total response-phase L&S hours from 172 to 24 per month (−86%); 4 post-change calls (0.2%) needed L&S transport, only 1 requiring advanced interventions

papers.title: Mobile ECPR team cannulates on scene
papers.n: 20 adults with witnessed refractory OHCA
papers.finding: Primary endpoint is collapse-to-ECMO flow time (target ≥15 min shorter than in-hospital ECPR), tested against historical and contemporaneous in-hospital cohorts; results not yet available

papers.title: Cardiac arrest systems not ready in rural Pakistan
papers.design: Mixed-methods (exit interviews, facility readiness checklist, focus groups and interviews)
papers.n: 163 patient exit interviews and 7 hospitals
papers.finding: Defibrillators present in 2 of 7 hospitals but neither functional, laryngeal mask airways unavailable in all facilities, and satisfaction lowest for communication (26.4%) and financial aspects (31.3%)

papers.title: Why patients decline hypoglycaemia call-back programs
papers.n: 16 adults with diabetes after EMS-attended severe hypoglycaemia
papers.finding: Non-participation reasons: time constraints 56%, perceived lack of benefit 25%, privacy concerns or discomfort with home visits 25%

papers.title: Predicting outcomes in PEA cardiac arrest
papers.design: Nationwide registry cohort with time-dependent propensity score sequential matching
papers.n: 442,630 adults with OHCA and initial rhythm PEA
papers.finding: Witnessed arrest (RR 1.65) and prehospital ROSC (RR 23.31) predicted favourable neurological outcome at 1 month; rhythm conversion predicted good outcome in cardiac PEA but poor outcome in non-cardiac PEA (RR 0.73); apparent harm from adrenaline and advanced airway management attenuated after time-dependent adjustment

papers.title: Drone AI for mass-casualty triage
papers.design: System development with pilot accuracy testing
papers.n: Not reported (pilot under controlled indoor conditions)
papers.finding: The system measured four vital signs from drone imagery via video PPG, thermal imaging and neural networks, generated triage decision support, and transmitted casualty location, vitals and triage category to response teams and dispatch

papers.title: Australian alcohol harms keep rising
papers.design: Joinpoint regression analysis of multiple national indicator datasets
papers.n: 13 years of national Australian data across consumption, wastewater and harm measures
papers.finding: Survey and wastewater consumption measures declined from 2010 while rates of most alcohol-related harms, including ambulance attendances, increased substantially

papers.title: Interprofessional simulation shapes student identity
papers.design: Exploratory descriptive qualitative study (single focus group, reflexive thematic analysis)
papers.n: One focus group of undergraduate paramedic students
papers.finding: Two themes emerged — Negotiating Professional Authority and Preparing for Collaborative Practice — with students reporting the simulation reshaped how they enacted the paramedic role, particularly around advocacy, handover and assertive communication

papers.title: Race, Gender, and Survival: a Scoping Review of Disparities in ICU Post-Resuscitation Care and Neurological Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
papers.journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities
papers.finding: Scoping review of 15 studies found Black women in the US received less bystander CPR, slower emergency response, less ICU intervention and more early DNR/withdrawal decisions after OHCA, with the disparities compounding across the chain of survival.

papers.title: Establishing a regional prehospital whole blood program in a border community: the Trauma Regional Advisory Council-V initiative in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas
papers.finding: Implementation report describing how four Texas border counties built a regional prehospital whole blood program across eight domains — governance, MOUs, rotation systems, provider credentialing and grant-funded equipment for rural agencies.

papers.title: EMS response time and patient outcomes in high-acuity emergency responses: a Danish matched cohort study
papers.finding: Danish matched cohort of 171,708 highest-priority (A-level) responses in Region Zealand tested whether EMS response times affect outcomes — mortality did not rise with longer response times, and the longest-quartile group had lower 30-day (OR 0.87) and 2-day (OR 0.82) mortality than the shortest quartiles.

papers.title: Challenges of turning prehospital prediction of trauma-induced coagulopathy into early administration of tranexamic acid
papers.finding: Editorial using a prehospital machine-learning risk model for trauma-induced coagulopathy found medium- and higher-risk patients still frequently miss tranexamic acid within the 1-hour window, arguing better risk stratification should close the evidence-to-practice gap.

papers.title: Emergency Department Operational Measures Associated with EMS Redirection Activation and Duration
papers.finding: Single-centre New York study over 392 days found EMS ambulance redirection activated on 63.8% of days, with ED visit volume associated with activation and door-to-room time associated with both activation and cumulative duration — but boarding and admissions were not.

papers.title: Feedback device lifts paediatric ventilation quality
papers.n: 123 EMS clinicians across 5 agencies
papers.finding: Guideline-recommended tidal volume in 87% of breaths with feedback vs 16.2% without; rate adherence 88.6% vs 65%; mask leak <30% in 88.4% vs 80%

papers.title: TBI in first responders needs occupational pathways
papers.journal: The Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation
papers.n: 28 consensus recommendations across a multidisciplinary group
papers.finding: Substantial TBI burden in law enforcement, fire and EMS with persistent gaps in diagnosis, rehabilitation and duty-readiness; 28 recommendations spanning recognition, early assessment, return to duty and organisational policy

papers.title: Joint training lifts behavioural emergency confidence
papers.n: 750 attendees, 395 in the paired analysis
papers.finding: Self-efficacy rose from 3.16 to 3.54 (mean difference 0.39, 95% CI 0.34–0.44, dz 0.76) and cognition from 3.81 to 3.95; behavioural-emergency stigma rose slightly and substance-use stigma was unchanged

papers.title: Dispatcher training + volunteer app lifts bystander CPR
papers.n: 1,684 adults with non-traumatic OHCA across 14 French EMS agencies
papers.finding: Bystander CPR before EMS arrival rose from 61.4% to 70.9% (adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.09–2.19), with no improvement in survival to discharge or neurological outcome

papers.title: Real-time feedback tidies BVM ventilation in arrest
papers.n: 4,300 ventilations in 163 adults with OHCA
papers.finding: With feedback, insufflated volume fell within guideline range in 68% of ventilations vs 42%, dispersion dropped 35%, and leak volume was 12% lower (mean ratio 0.88); expired tidal volume was unchanged

papers.title: Fatigue common a year after cardiac arrest
papers.n: 728 OHCA survivors (68.2% of those eligible) interviewed at 12 months in Victoria
papers.finding: Fatigue 35.8%, anxiety 22.6%, depression 18.0%; fatigue exceeded population norms (SMD 0.64) and higher symptom burden tracked with worse EQ-5D, GOSE and return-to-work rates

papers.title: Keep pulse checks under 5 seconds
papers.n: 252 cardiac arrest patients (124 with ≤5-second checks, 128 with 6–10-second checks)
papers.finding: Shorter pulse checks were linked to higher ROSC (36.3% vs 19.5%; OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.35–4.24) and more favourable ETCO2 loss and recovery patterns

papers.title: Pad application is the AED time bottleneck
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of remotely monitored AED timestamps
papers.n: 8,115 AED activation events (900 initially shock-advised with recorded shock)
papers.finding: Median power-on-to-pad-application was 42 seconds, accounting for 81% of the power-on-to-first-analysis interval; a threshold of ≥51 seconds identified shock delivery beyond 60 seconds

papers.title: Whole blood on ambulances: first two years
papers.n: Patients transfused low-titre O-positive whole blood by paramedics across two US cities, Dec 2022–Feb 2025
papers.finding: Systolic blood pressure, heart rate and shock index improved significantly after transfusion, and improved systolic blood pressure carried 9.7-fold greater odds of survival to hospital arrival

papers.title: Physician-directed ALS: no survival gain
papers.n: 129,207 adults with OHCA across South Korea
papers.finding: SALS regions gained prehospital ROSC (+1.35 pp, 95% CI 0.56–2.15) but not survival to discharge (−0.35 pp) or favourable neurological outcome, while prehospital time rose 4.12 minutes

papers.title: Mass casualty care: slower but no deadlier
papers.n: 423 severely injured MCI patients matched to 1,692 controls
papers.finding: Median prehospital time was 85 vs 67 minutes; prehospital intubation (33.6% vs 20.9%) and TXA (32.1% vs 15.0%) were more frequent, but in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly

papers.title: Prehospital flumazenil: 69 doses, no seizures
papers.journal: The Western Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 69 prehospital flumazenil administrations over five years
papers.finding: No seizures or adverse events were associated with flumazenil use (0/69; 95% CI 0–4.3%), with GCS improvement in the treated cases

papers.title: OHCA registry clock times run short
papers.n: 56,969 OHCA registry records linked to dispatch data, 2015–2024
papers.finding: Unit response time differed by a median 0.3 seconds between sources, but total response time was systematically 80.9 seconds shorter in the registry, with large regional variation

papers.title: Resilience as a skill, not a trait
papers.n: 20 Queensland paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2–38 years)
papers.finding: Three intensifiers (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) and three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) emerged, with work mode showing features of skilled performance

papers.title: Bathroom jobs eat scene time
papers.n: 26,058 people aged ≥65 transported from home over nine years
papers.finding: On-scene time was longer for toilets (aMR 1.08), bathrooms (1.09) and kitchens (1.06) versus living rooms, shorter in corridors and gardens (both 0.95), and rose with floor level

papers.title: POC troponin on ambulances: fewer ED visits
papers.n: 737 patients with suspected ACS from the French VALIDATE cohort
papers.finding: ED attendance fell 5.8 percentage points (90.9% vs 96.7%, p<0.001) and mean ED stay dropped from 2.76 to 1.63 hours with prehospital hs-cTnI

papers.title: Decision support eases stroke triage load
papers.journal: The Western Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 35 EMT-intermediate participants, two 12-minute simulated trials each
papers.finding: RMSSD rose from 28.1 to 32.4 ms (mean difference 4.3 ms, 95% CI 1.57–6.99) and mean heart rate fell with decision support, indicating lower mental workload

papers.title: Dutch TEAM tool validated for resus training
papers.n: 52 participant groups, 104 observed team performances, 299 instructor ratings
papers.finding: Internal consistency was high (α 0.93), three-rater reliability good (ICC 0.78) and the total score correlated strongly with global ratings (r 0.86), though ceiling effects affected all items

papers.title: Infant carry slings rarely linked to OHCA
papers.n: 162 children under two who received a resuscitation attempt
papers.finding: Only 2 of 162 OHCA were carry sling-associated (1.8% of the 114 infant cases); co-sleeping accounted for 33.3% and children found unresponsive 26.3%

papers.title: No unique GCS 8 threshold for intubation
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 138,405 adults transported directly from scene (71,988 + 66,417)
papers.finding: Recorded intubation was 9.1–10.6 percentage points more frequent at GCS 8 (pooled aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.36–1.91), but model fit favoured a graded GCS–outcome relationship over a discrete jump at the 8/9 boundary in every outcome and both eras

papers.title: Paediatric deterioration in the field poorly defined
papers.n: 28 studies published 1990–2026, mostly retrospective and from high-income countries
papers.finding: No study offered an operational definition of paediatric out-of-hospital deterioration; research leans on single-timepoint vital signs, trauma-specific indices and hospital-derived early warning scores, and no study examined physiological trajectories

papers.title: Paediatric care coordinators linked to fewer EMS errors
papers.n: 2,219 paediatric encounters across 15 EMS agencies, 2019–2023
papers.finding: Coordinator agencies performed more procedures (55.4% vs 26.8%) and gave more medications (23.4% vs 7.7%); procedure adverse safety event rates were 13.7% vs 20.0%, with lower assigned harm severity

papers.title: AU/NZ emergency care research priorities being set
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: No results yet — the partnership is underway, aiming to prioritise unanswered questions across the ~11 million annual ED presentations in both countries

papers.title: Who doesn't call an ambulance for chest pain
papers.n: 14 Australian studies
papers.finding: EMS use for ACS ranged 36–79%; under-49s up to 68% lower odds of EMS use than over-65s, men up to 11% lower than women, overseas-born up to 15% lower, non-English speakers 6–20% lower, remote residents up to 25% lower than major-city residents

papers.title: Prehospital ultrasound as a decision tool
papers.design: Structured narrative review (38 articles, 9 systematic reviews)
papers.n: 38 articles reviewed
papers.finding: POCUS may identify cardiac activity and reversible causes in arrest, characterise shock mechanisms and improve diagnostic confidence in cardiogenic pulmonary oedema; E-FAST has high specificity but limited sensitivity so it cannot be used as a rule-out test

papers.title: How Utah widened paramedic oxytocin scope
papers.design: Community-based interprofessional quality improvement initiative (implementation science framework)
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: State EMS protocols changed in April 2024 to allow paramedic oxytocin for PPH prevention and AEMT intramuscular oxytocin for PPH prevention and treatment

papers.title: HEMS vs road: guideline adherence in trauma
papers.journal: European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery
papers.n: 129,783 adults with severe trauma (25% HEMS)
papers.finding: HEMS transport associated with higher intervention rates across all indication-based subgroups: advanced airway in impaired consciousness 96.5% vs 82.9%, chest tube placement 50.5% vs 40.9%, despite HEMS patients being younger and more severely injured

papers.title: Paramedics on digital decision support
papers.design: Exploratory qualitative interview study (reflexive thematic analysis)
papers.n: 12 paramedics interviewed
papers.finding: Four themes: digital support for call assessment and ambulance resource allocation, digital patient information for shared situational awareness, digital communication for interprofessional consultation, and implementation challenges despite established prehospital infrastructure

papers.title: Cluster trials read differently to individual ones
papers.n: 65 meta-analyses, 212 RCTs (39 cluster), 315,276 patients
papers.finding: No statistically significant difference in mortality effect estimates between cluster and individually randomised trials (MD lnOR −0.110, 95% CI −0.093 to 0.313); cluster trials showed significantly smaller effect magnitudes for length-of-stay/days-alive outcomes (Hedges' g MD −0.202, 95% CI −0.392 to −0.012)

papers.title: Hot days drive dizziness call-outs
papers.n: 270,120 emergency transports, 8,981 dizziness-related
papers.finding: Higher mean air temperature consistently associated with increased odds of high-frequency dizziness-transport days (≥5/day), as were short-term maximum-temperature increases and smaller diurnal temperature ranges; most frequent in summer

papers.title: Hot nights linked to more OHCA
papers.n: 135,898 emergency hospitalisations for OHCA
papers.finding: Nighttime heat exposure increased OHCA hospitalisation (RR 1.090, 95% CI 1.047–1.135); RR rose to 1.295 in people ≥75 and 1.352 in women in northern regions, and risk was higher where air-conditioning penetration was low

papers.title: ECPR for OHCA: pump the brakes
papers.design: Narrative review/commentary of three randomised ECPR trials
papers.n: Three RCTs (ARREST n=30, INCEPTION, Prague OHCA)
papers.finding: Only ARREST (30 patients) strongly favoured ECPR; INCEPTION and Prague OHCA were not statistically significant, and the authors argue intra-arrest transport effects cannot be excluded as a driver of reported benefit

papers.title: How ambulance models shape end-of-life care
papers.design: Embedded qualitative case study of three English ambulance service models, framework analysis
papers.n: 101 participants (75 healthcare professionals, 26 patients and carers) across 3 services
papers.finding: Learning on the job and limited access to records, anticipatory medicines and palliative advice dominated practice across all three models; paramedic workload was driven partly by primary and community service shortages

papers.title: Scene-to-door time and stroke thrombectomy
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort, comprehensive stroke centre (2018–2023)
papers.n: 121 patients transported directly from scene to EVT
papers.finding: In patients with pre-stroke disability (mRS ≥1), longer scene-to-door time independently reduced favourable 90-day outcome (adjusted OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.81–0.98; optimal cutoff 14 min); no significant association in the overall cohort (AUC 0.57)

papers.title: Kratom derivative withdrawal treated prehospital
papers.design: Case series, US community paramedic buprenorphine program
papers.n: 2 patients
papers.finding: Buprenorphine 24 mg and 32 mg/8 mg with naloxone treated severe 7-OH/MGM-15 withdrawal; both patients were linked to outpatient treatment within 48 hours and retained in treatment at 30 days

papers.title: HEMS burnout high even without PTSD
papers.n: 73 physicians, HEMS crew paramedics and pilots (89% response rate)
papers.finding: 48.6% exceeded the personal burnout cutoff, 23.2% work-related and 17.4% patient-related; no one met PTSD criteria; trauma exposure correlated with PTSD symptoms (r=0.30) and work-related burnout (r=0.33)

papers.title: Neonatal calls rare on South African ambulances
papers.design: Retrospective review of electronic patient care records, 2022–2023
papers.n: 9,825 neonatal activations
papers.finding: Neonatal activations were 0.7% of EMS workload; prehospital intubation 0.4%; recorded mechanical ventilation 4.6% versus sedation/analgesia 1.1%; specialist retrieval teams were strongly associated with advanced interventions

papers.title: Paramedics under-document neuro change over time
papers.n: 348 paramedics
papers.finding: Mean self-reported documentation completeness 24.57/35; level of consciousness was documented often (81.0%) but only 9.2% consistently documented temporal neurological changes; training was associated with higher scores (26.20 vs 23.24, P<0.001)

papers.title: Eye-tracking shows how experience guides ambulance care
papers.design: Cross-sectional observational study, wearable eye-tracking in real ambulance transfers
papers.n: 9 flight nurses across 60 cases
papers.finding: Four principal components of gaze behaviour (fixation count, visit count, fixation duration) were significantly associated with experience group after adjustment for multiple comparisons; novices showed distinctly different fixation patterns from experts

papers.title: Why rural stroke care lags: system drivers
papers.design: Qualitative service evaluation, semi-structured interviews with system stakeholders, thematic analysis
papers.n: 11 stakeholders (paramedics, stroke nurses, GPs, managers, a neurologist, a researcher)
papers.finding: Inequity emerged where stroke recognition had to convert rapidly into dispatch priority, on-scene capability, pre-alerting and transfer; rural and coastal distance compounded delay when combined with limited patient mobility, complex extrication and Category 2 demand

papers.title: Clearer AED voice prompts fix lay-user errors
papers.design: Simulation-based before/after assessment with a manikin
papers.n: 81 final-year dental students
papers.finding: With standard AED instructions, fewer than 10% of students correctly completed 8 of 10 assessed items (median time to shock 143 s); modified instructions significantly improved device activation and later steps (P<0.001)
